launches.title: Ryhla: Faster power grid connection for your project
launches.tagline: Data and models of the distribution grid
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Ryhla gets projects connected to the power grid. Our proprietary models replicate the distribution grid, and we use them to take projects through interconnection end to end. Developers typically get 20 to 40% of applications approved. Our models got 91%.** 

<https://youtu.be/e-qtjw-T0M0>

**The problem**\
Today, a developer files an interconnection request (the application to plug a project into the grid) and waits months for the utility’s answer. Too often it’s a rejection or a massive upgrade bill, after the time and money are already spent. Unlike transmission, where queues and capacity maps are often public, the distribution grid is a black box.

**What we do**\
We built proprietary models that replicate how the distribution grid behaves and how utilities decide what gets connected. Today, developers use them to drop dead projects early and shape the ones that can work into applications that get approved. For each project, we know how much capacity is available (for load and injection), how to size it, how long it will take and what the upgrade would cost. Then we handle the interconnection end to end.

**Results**

* We’re live with one of the biggest solar developers in the Midwest.
* 91% of the sites our models said yes to were approved by the utility (2025 distribution-level applications).
* We saved a battery developer about $160k in fees by ruling out 8 of their 10 planned projects in a few days.

**Why now**

* **Grid demand is exploding.** Data centers, EV chargers, batteries, new factories: everything is plugging into the grid at once, and utilities can’t keep up with the requests.
* **Projects are moving to the distribution grid.** Transmission queues take years, so more and more projects connect at the distribution level instead, where public data is often missing.
* **The opportunity is massive.** More power capacity is waiting in line to connect than all the power plants in the US combined, and every one of those projects has to go through interconnection.

**Who we are**\
We're Sara (CEO) and Yassine (CTO). We've been best friends since middle school and both grew up in Morocco, a country betting big on solar, which is how we got hooked on energy. We studied electrical and computational engineering at École Polytechnique, then did research on grid intelligence models at Stanford, which became Ryhla. We first deployed our models with utilities, so we know how interconnection works on their side. 

**Asks**

* Intros to developers building on the distribution grid: solar, storage, community solar, C&I, EV charging, small data centers. 
* **Have a project that needs a grid connection? Send it to founders@ryhla.ai**
